newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products firm, gas oil much stronger.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products firm, gas oil much stronger.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were firm on Thursday, with gas oil the star performer.
Gasoline was stable with futures. While a little low octane material was thought to be still available, other barrels were hard to come by. But demand was not robust either.

Naphtha remains firm, after the sale of a Skikda cargo on Wednesday at $4.50 a tonne over the quoted cif high. Few cargoes are seen on offer and petrochemical demand remains healthy, given the high price of alternative feedstocks.
Gas oil prices jumped another $7.00 on Thursday in line with IPE gains and extremely strong demand for diesel fuel and gas oil with good cold properties.
Traders said some of the 400,000 tonnes of U.S. material coming to Europe was being offered actively and hardly seemed to dampen sentiment.
Good quality Russian was bid at October +$5.00 and offered at least as high as $6.00 premium cif Augusta, but a FOD cargo was finding little buying interest at Oct +$3.50 cif Genoa, dealers said.

The Greek tender to buy 600,000 tonnes of gas oil for delivery October-March was still unclear, although Glencore, Neopetro and Statoil were thought to have won most of it at around benchmark quotes high flat to high +$1.00 cif. A company called Transax was also thought to have secured a small amount.
A Greek PPC source said on Thursday that 0.05 percent sulphur diesel would be introduced at the pumps in Greece by January 1, three months late. The status of Portugal is unclear.
Bunker quality fuel oil remained sought after. Burning quality product saw an Italian buyer looking into Naples, but so far was still uncovered.
